fluff.overview:
The Peacekeeper is a ninety-five-ton assault BattleMech developed in the aftermath of the Jihad as a joint venture between the newly-formed Republic of the Sphere and the Draconis Combine. First produced in 3086, the design was conceived as a gesture of trust between the two nations, intended for anti-insurgency operations and garrison duty. The project mandated a lack of proprietary technology, ensuring both realms could independently construct and maintain the chassis without reliance on the other.

The Peacekeeper established itself as a capable garrison platform, with its formidable energy-based firepower and considerable operational endurance proving well-suited to sustained field operations. Production was established at Independence Weaponry on Quentin and Luthien Armor Works on New Samarkand, and the design has continued to serve both nations well into the ilClan era.
fluff.capabilities:
The Peacekeeper was designed as a heavy garrison 'Mech capable of sustained field operations without regular resupply, a requirement that drove the emphasis on energy-based weaponry with minimal ammunition dependency. At ninety-five tons, the chassis is powered by a GM 380 XL engine providing a top speed of sixty-five kilometers per hour, surprisingly quick for its weight class. Triple Strength Myomer further augments this mobility when the 'Mech runs hot, potentially pushing speeds to eighty-six kilometers per hour. Three Lexington Ltd. Lifters jump jets give the Peacekeeper a ninety-meter jump capability, providing tactical flexibility unusual in an assault design.

The primary armament centers on twin particle projection cannons (a Lord's Light 3 Heavy PPC and a Lord's Light 2 Extended Range PPC) delivering devastating long-range firepower. A Victory Nickel Alloy ER Large Laser supplements these primary weapons, while a Victory Blast Furnace Plasma Rifle inflicts both damage and significant heat buildup on its targets, discouraging close engagement. A Guided Technologies SRM-2 launcher rounds out the armament as a concession to anti-infantry work. Eighteen tons of standard armor provide solid protection for the massive frame, complemented by a CASE system to mitigate ammunition explosions. The integration of a C3 computer enables the Peacekeeper to share targeting data with lancemates, enhancing the effectiveness of combined arms operations.
fluff.history:
The Peacekeeper's origins lie in the tumultuous aftermath of the Jihad, when the Republic of the Sphere sought to reassure the Draconis Combine that the concession of worlds from former Combine territory was not a slight to be left unaddressed. A joint BattleMech development program was proposed as a concrete gesture of trust between the two nascent allies, with the fundamental requirement that neither nation's proprietary technology would be used, ensuring both could independently produce and maintain the design without dependency on the other.

Development proceeded rapidly despite the ongoing Jihad, with prototype testing beginning while combat still raged across the Inner Sphere. Five mercenary units were commissioned to conduct field evaluations, selected for their assignments in active combat zones, particularly those focused on pirate hunting duties. Their reports proved largely positive, and the mercenaries retained their Peacekeepers as compensation for service. Full production was authorized for both Independence Weaponry on Quentin and Luthien Armor Works on New Samarkand, with manufacturing commencing in mid-to-late 3086.

The Peacekeeper entered active service during the Early Republic era, seeing deployment across both Republic and Combine territories. Independence Weaponry's Quentin facility, which had passed through numerous hands over the centuries (including the Terran Hegemony, Federated Suns, Draconis Combine, and Word of Blake) produced the design under Republic oversight before the world transitioned through a period of independence and ultimately returned to Combine control. The Luthien Armor Works facility on New Samarkand remained firmly in Combine hands throughout, providing consistent production capacity.

By the Dark Age, the Peacekeeper had established itself as a capable garrison platform across Combine space. The introduction of the PKP-2K in 3116 reflected the DCMS's ongoing efforts to integrate advanced electronics and improved armor technologies into their front-line designs. The original purpose of the Peacekeeper as a symbol of inter-state cooperation had long since faded by this period, replaced by its practical value as a heavy garrison 'Mech with formidable energy-based firepower and considerable operational endurance. Despite the dissolution of the Republic of the Sphere, the design continued to serve the Combine well into the ilClan era.
fluff.deployment: This variant emerged in 3116 as a Draconis Combine-exclusive evolution of the Peacekeeper, produced solely at Luthien Armor Works on New Samarkand. This variant replaces the ER Large Laser with a medium X-pulse laser, trading long-range supplementary firepower for improved close-range accuracy. The most significant change is the adoption of anti-penetrative ablation armor, offering enhanced resistance to certain advanced weapon types at the cost of conventional ballistic protection. Installation of a C3 Emergency Master computer was intended to establish a new command standard for Peacekeeper formations, allowing the 'Mech to assume network coordination duties. However, the DCMS's gradual shift toward boosted C3 systems in favor of conventional networks ultimately curtailed widespread adoption of this configuration.
